_comment: Accepted-and-triaged dependency advisories, as of the Trust Release final assurance pass (see SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_DEBT.md's 'Pass 3'). scripts/check_dependency_baseline.py fails CI if pip-audit reports an advisory for a package not listed here, or a new advisory ID for a listed package that isn't in its accepted list — either means something changed and needs re-triage, not a silent pass.

black.reason: Dev-only formatter, never imported by application code (grep -rn '^import black|^from black' outside tests/scripts is empty).

pytest.reason: Dev/CI-only, never imported by application code. The one open advisory (CVE-2025-71176) also requires local multi-user access to the machine running the suite, which is not this app's threat model.

cryptography.reason: cryptography is imported directly (services/connect/credentials.py's Fernet, utils/wallet_passes.py's hazmat.primitives/x509 for Apple Wallet pass signing). All 3 CVEs (PYSEC-2026-3552 PKCS7 decrypt oracle, -3553 x509 chain-build DoS, -3554 x509.verification DNS-wildcard bypass) are in cryptography.x509.verification/pkcs7_decrypt_* APIs that grep confirms this codebase never calls (no PolicyBuilder/x509.verification/pkcs7_decrypt/.verify( usage). GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf (bundled OpenSSL advisory) is accepted pending the deferred 46->48->49->50 major-version walk documented in SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_DEBT.md.

starlette.reason: Imported directly by server.py/middleware for BaseHTTPMiddleware/CORSMiddleware/JSONResponse. Version is structurally pinned by fastapi==0.110.1's own metadata (starlette<0.38.0,>=0.37.2); closing these requires a coordinated FastAPI bump, tracked separately. PYSEC-2026-161 (Host-header path-injection auth-bypass) was the one advisory in this set with a confirmed, exploitable, in-app impact (RequireAuthMiddleware's request.url.path check) -- fixed directly at the application layer in this pass (server.py/middleware/license_middleware.py/services/observability.py now read request.scope['path']) rather than waiting on the framework bump, so it no longer represents live risk regardless of when starlette itself is upgraded. The remaining 6 (two multipart-form DoS, two low-severity misc) are accepted pending the same FastAPI bump.
